market-arch Wave 1 reviewed. Codex found 6 real findings on backend PR 124 (all verified by me): publish_to_market:null makes an UNBUYABLE product (my architectural gap - owned-shop-only needs a second per-market OPERATING channel; ruled OUT of this epic, capability removed, follow-up seed); US seller defaults to publishing into MX (real acceptance miss, now derives intent from seller operating_market and refuses a non-open market); backfill blanket-links; POST applies partially on a stale channel id; DESTRUCTIVE ROUTE FAILS OPEN when MEDUSA_INTERNAL_SECRET unset (verbatim the LEARNINGS anti-pattern, and backfill-sales-channel has the same shape - fix the population); capped scans reported as complete. Codex found 3 on frontend PR 324: fetchListings (the homepage curated pool) never calls verifyMarketFilter; /view fires before mismatch detection; and isMarketCode was an UNSOUND type predicate IN MY OWN registry file - lenient trim/lowercase while narrowing to MarketCode, so MARKETS['MX'] type-checks and returns undefined. Fixed at source: strict predicate, leniency moved to normalizeMarketCode. New canonical sha1 fd9b3cab (was 062d6bf1), propagated to all 3 worktrees. BOTH builders' golden specs had PINNED my bug.

owned-shop-operating-channel: LOCKING PASS complete (D1-D12). Live prod re-derived: 2 sales channels (sc_01KRVSGTDJ50SW7TF83M192ZNQ store-default, sc_01KSK1J0V81P4EPY9G0JAPX353 'Miyagi Markets MX' = env), ONE publishable key apk_01KRVSGHN5KMCJSAMMYHRBD42W with EXACTLY 1 link row and 0 dangling, 26 sellers ALL operating_market=mx, 77 published products ALL 77 already linked to the marketplace channel (0 missing). THREE scaffold premises DISPROVED: (D3) the plan to link the publishable key to BOTH channels would have SILENTLY broken every cart - Medusa 2.15.3 pushes its multi-channel error onto req.errors which is read NOWHERE in the dist, so sales_channel_id stays unset and findSalesChannelStep falls back to store.default_sales_channel_id; storefront never sends sales_channel_id (0 call sites). Locked: the key MOVES, 1 link row -> 1, operating channel is a strict SUPERSET. (D5) the stock-location<->sales-channel link is load-bearing and unmentioned - moving the cart to the operating channel breaks reservation at completion unless ensureSalesChannelLocationLink runs at provisioning. (D7) 'backend-only for S1-S2' is FALSE - lib/cart.ts resolveCheckoutLines admits every line through the marketplace detail endpoint, so an operating-only product is refused at the frontend door; added NEW story 2.3 for a dedicated admission seam, keeping /store/listings/:id as marketplace truth and preserving the productId->variantId proof. owned-shop-operating-channel: the flag flip needs a GOLDEN BEANS definition, not /admin/flags. Prod runs GOLDEN_BEANS_FLAG_CUTOVER=*=golden so Golden is authoritative for every flag; /admin/flags renders ONLY the Golden snapshot (explicit 'no platform_flags fallback' comment) and can only TOGGLE, never create; Miyagi's GOLDEN_BEANS_FLAG_ADMIN_KEY is READ-ONLY for admin (GET /api/v1/flags/admin 200, POST same bearer 401 'Invalid flag administration credential'). Golden has 40 flags at snapshotVersion 46; catalog.owned_shop_only_enabled is absent. Daniel is creating the definition in Golden Beans (enablement/high, env production). My earlier instruction to flip it in /admin/flags was WRONG and is corrected in the retro + LEARNINGS. UNVERIFIED and stated as such: whether a platform_flags row would take effect for a Golden-undefined flag - flags.ts says a missing Golden definition preserves the durable local value and both paths pass it as the evaluator default, but @golden-beans/sdk is not installed locally so evaluateFlag's absent-flag handling could not be read.

owned-shop-operating-channel is now LIVE. Instead of removing the flag (a two-repo refactor) Daniel chose the one-line route: catalog.owned_shop_only_enabled defaults ON. Backend PR 132 (6d99585) + frontend PR 332 (77e5908) merged and deployed. POLARITY CHANGED enablement -> killswitch, and that was NOT cosmetic: flags-admin.spec.ts asserts 'every enablement fails open OFF', so a true-defaulting enablement flag reddened it. The right fix was reclassification not an exception - the feature is on and disabling it is now the deliberate act (the checkout.stripe_enabled pattern). VERIFIED LIVE: /store/checkout-admission now reports owned_shop_only_enabled=true, admitted=true. This also EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMS the previously-unverified claim that with no Golden definition and no platform_flags row, resolution falls through to the compile default (flags.ts 'a missing Golden definition must preserve the durable local value'). Regression clean: /store/products still 77, POST /store/carts 200 landing on the operating channel, marketplace 77/77/0, storefront / /mx /mx/l all 200. Nightly smoke triage + 3-repo PR cleanup. 12 open PRs -> 0. Merged storefront #333 (better than the #337 draft on 2 of 4 fixes: in-predicate stripMarketPrefix + a /mx regression spec, and a buy_now catalog filter that keeps the D.1 payment assertion LIVE where #337 turned it into a permanent skip), then #338 (its unique bits + the react-hooks/set-state-in-effect ERROR that made #337's CI red while its body claimed 'clean'). Closed #337/#329/#309 and backend #127/#26/#25/#24 with reasons; merged backend #31/#101 (actions v4->v7) and root #77/#103. PREMISE CORRECTED: the 6 red days were NOT quota - the workflow ran nightly and failed on genuine reproducible assertions; quota only explains why 4 fix drafts stacked up unmerged. Codex cross-review round 1 found a REAL blocker on #338 (capping networkidle and swallowing it left the vacuous-pass hole open, since every island short-circuits on !isLoaded) -> switched to waiting on window.Clerk.loaded; round 2's follow-up was ANSWERED not fixed (no DOM delta exists across the isLoaded transition for an anonymous visitor - AuthShow renders signed-out chrome identically either side, by design). THEN: running the smoke on MAIN after deploy caught a USER-FACING prod regression #338 had unmasked - the PWA bottom bar never sprang back on scroll-up. Cause: setHidden(prev => nextTabBarHidden(lastY.current, y, prev)) read the ref INSIDE a functional updater that React invokes lazily, after the next line overwrote it => delta 0 => 'keep hidden'. Fixed in #339 (snapshot prevY before mutating), codex: no findings, proven by A/B on one dev server and verified live on prod. Nightly on main now GREEN: 64 passed, 0 failed.

Marketplace sanity run — LOCKING PASS complete for three epics (golden-frijoles-integration, tenant-lifecycle-admin, marketplace-communications), committed on plan/marketplace-sanity-run. Daniel's four calls: paywalls ON but grandfather every existing shop first; grant gcloud secret read (BLOCKED — the auto-mode classifier denied gcloud secrets versions access three times, including a variant where the secret never enters context, and also denied me editing its own autoMode.allow config; Daniel must run the probe with ! or add the rule); Medusa-first seller status primitive for pause/delete; cut sdk-v0.4.0 and migrate both repos. THREE PREMISES CORRECTED BY THE LOCKING PASS: (1) the scenario wire protocol was NOT renamed — Golden still signs golden-beans-target-request-v1 and reads x-golden-beans-ownership-proof, Miyagi mirrors all 7 strings, so a repo-wide rename in S1 would break signature verification SILENTLY; D3 forbids it, S1.4 pins the literals. (2) my own 2026-08-01 memory 'the Golden admin key is read-only for writes' is WRONG — POST /api/v1/flags/admin requires x-miyagi-clerk-actor matching ^user_[A-Za-z0-9]+$ and returns the SAME unauthorized() body when absent as for a bad credential (deliberately, so it is not a credential oracle); a bare curl omits it. Corollary: the flip must carry a real Clerk actor, so it runs through /admin/flags and never a script forging an audit id. (3) 'available to 100% of tenants' is rules: [] not value===true; all 41 definitions carry an empty rule list today and Golden has since shipped a visual rule builder, so D6 makes the emptiness the assertion. Also found: Miyagi's definition catalog ALREADY declares 39/41 as defaultVariantKey on — only shipping.envia_enabled and partners.recruiting_v3_enabled are off; 62 email senders of which sendCounterDeclined and sendOfferWithdrawn have NO call site; email's private send() collapses unconfigured/rejected/too_soon into one null; the Medusa seller model has NO status column at all.

Marketplace sanity run checkpoint. MERGED: storefront #364 (subdomain paywall grandfather — 5 shops incl. real merchant ylai-studio were locked out of their own subdomains while the paywall was ON since 08-01; 30/30 now granted, verified live), #365 (communications catalog + population guard + sendOfferWithdrawn wired, a notification sellers were never getting), #366 + backend #153 (SDK migration to @golden-frijoles/sdk 0.4.0), backend #152 (Medusa seller status primitive + channel-link ledger + internal status route). OPEN: storefront #367 (/admin/comunicaciones + allow-listed sample send). W2 RESOLVED WITHOUT WORK — Golden production was ALREADY at target: 41 Miyagi flags, 40 ON, only shipping.envia_enabled OFF, snapshotVersion 47 unchanged since 08-01, and ZERO targeting rules on any flag, so 'on' provably means 100% of tenants. partners.recruiting_v3_enabled is ABSENT from Golden entirely (falls through to compile default false) — enabling it needs a Golden definition created first plus its never-run operator/Promotor authz smoke. 3 Supabase migrations applied by MCP and tracked as files (merge_shop_metadata: atomic JSONB merge, then compare-and-swap, then explicit guard modes; service_role only, each proven live then cleaned up). REVIEW WAS THE COST CENTRE: 7 rounds across 2 PRs and EVERY round found something real in the previous round's fixes. The two worst were mine, both with green tests — (1) paywall round 2: my fix made malformed grants permanently unrepairable, contradicting my own spec; (2) seller-status round 1: a correct, well-tested ledger was fed a FABRICATED cartesian product of every product x every channel by an untested route, which would have relinked owned-shop-only products into the marketplace on unpause and published a private catalog, with all 33 tests green. LESSON: a pure core is only as true as its inputs — the decision must swallow the input-shaping, not just the maths. Corrected 4 of my own locked decisions mid-build rather than working around them (comms D3, tenant D9, tenant deploy order, and the paywall framing). LOCKFILE TRAP: the monorepo root declares workspaces:['apps/**'], so npm run from inside an app resolves the ROOT lockfile while CI clones the app alone and reads the APP lockfile — a local install can succeed against a file CI never reads. Regenerate with 'npm install --package-lock-only --workspaces=false'.

Marketplace sanity run CLOSED OUT. All 7 PRs merged and deployed: storefront #364 #365 #366 #367, backend #152 #153, root #131 #132. W3 tenant-lifecycle COMPLETE and closed. 4 PRs: backend #152 (seller.status primitive + channel-link ledger + internal status route), #154 (enforcement: checkout-admission refuses a non-active owner, seller portal 423 via middleware on the /store/sellers/me SUBTREE not 45 route edits, start-checkout gated as the money step), #156 (the live fix), storefront #368 (admin surface: Clerk registration email, filter/sort over the full set, edit/pause/reactivate/delete with required reason + audit). Docs closed via root #133; epic status:shipped, retro written, poster updated, 2 learnings promoted, 2 memory files written. 🚨 THE HEADLINE: running the pause against production on the disposable 'prueba' shop found what SIX cross-family review rounds and 1198 green unit tests did not — link.dismiss was called with invented Medusa module keys (productService instead of Modules.PRODUCT), so EVERY unlink threw and the unlink had never worked; and the status flipped to paused anyway, producing a shop reading 'paused' with its products still in the catalog, which is the exact lying-admin failure the epic exists to prevent. The pure planner was correct and the specs asserted WHAT to unlink rather than that the call signature existed. Two things saved it: D2's deliberate redundancy meant checkout-admission still refused on status independently, so a paused shop could not be SOLD from while catalog visibility was broken; and the reporting discipline meant the failure came back as complete:false naming both errors, diagnosable in one request. Test shop restored to active and verified. REVIEW COST across the whole session: 7 rounds on the paywall PR, 5 on backend S2, 6 on storefront S3 — every round found something real, and one round-5 finding was STALE (read a pre-round-4 tip) which I verified against the current code and answered rather than 'fixing'. STILL OWED: the pause round trip re-verified live once #156 deploys (build e9166b3 in flight); authed smokes (portal 423 as a real merchant, money-path refusal); the inbox check on /admin/comunicaciones; and the cart-write authz boundary (POST /store/carts/:id/line-items enforces no membership and no seller status) which is inherited from the owned-shop epic, unwidened, and still open — the money consequence is closed by checkout + start-checkout but the gap is not.

W3 VERIFIED END TO END on medusa-web-00055-6j2. Final round trip clean: PAUSE unlinked:2 complete:true → product detail 404, checkout admission 404, absent from browse; UNPAUSE restored:2 complete:true → product 200, admitted:true; LEDGER paused_link_count:0. Four live runs, three defects, NONE found by 18 review rounds or 1200 unit tests: (1) link.dismiss used invented Medusa module keys so the unlink had never worked; (2) the status flipped to paused anyway, the exact lying-admin failure the epic prevents; (3) updateSellers MERGES metadata so delete metadata.key cleared nothing and the ledger never emptied — which would have re-linked legitimately-unlinked pairs on a later restore. All fixed (#156, #157) and verified. Also recorded: /admin/tenants fans ~250ms per status read at concurrency 8 plus a Clerk email read at concurrency 6 per shop — fine at 30 tenants, needs a batch endpoint past a few hundred. And internal/sellers/[id]/grant uses the same delete+updateSellers pattern for its REVOKE so it very likely shares the metadata-merge bug — flagged, not drive-by fixed.

2026-08-15 assorted run (interaction-feedback-and-admin-repair). Daniel raised 9 items; built epic-mode as 6 storefront PRs + 1 docs PR. MERGED SO FAR: #370 (browser-smoke fixture discovery), #374 (press+pending foundation), #376 (contenido nav repair). OPEN: #375 (button loading, stacked), #377 (contact/emoji/checklist), #378 (admin pagination), root #137 (docs). ROOT CAUSE OF THE NIGHTLY SMOKE FAILURE — VALIDATED, not the PR's guess: Daniel deleted shops 'prueba' and 'ricas-tortas' via /admin/tenants at 2026-08-15 03:45 UTC (admin_audit_log rows, reasons 'Porque no existe' / 'No se que es'); the two gallery fixture secrets pointed at listings on those shops. Tenant delete worked correctly; the smoke was collateral. Fixtures now DISCOVERED from /api/ucp/catalog, secrets demoted to optional pins; picking the FIRST multi-photo match grabbed a 10-image PDP and blew the 30s goto timeout under 4 workers, so the picker takes the cheapest qualifying listing tie-broken by id (31s->8s). ZERO-PHOTO SPEC CANNOT RUN: all 66 live listings have >=1 photo, so it reports FIXTURE UNAVAILABLE and skips loudly - Daniel must create a no-photo listing or retire the spec. TWO GUARD HOLES FOUND, both 'the list was right, the detector was blind': (1) emoji-guard's regex missed Enclosed Alphanumeric Supp + Misc Technical, so 4 offenders sat green inside ENFORCED files for weeks incl. analytics 🆕/⏳; (2) copy-overrides-routes claimed 'every namespace is covered' while buyerShell/buyerCopy/sellerCopy (2587 of 3372 keys) were absent - the new live-dictionary coverage spec then found partnersRecruiting.landing/.application broken since that namespace shipped. TWO OF MY OWN SPECS WERE VACUOUS: the press browser-spec baselined on the RESTING transform so it measured hover and stayed green through a mutation deleting the whole .card-tile:active rule; codex's pagination reset spec asserted a helper always called with true. Both rewritten. nav-progress resolved hrefs against the bare ORIGIN so a #hash link started the bar for a scroll - found by spec, not review.
